decision.summary: The Federal Reserve voted to keep the target range for the federal funds rate at 1 to 1-1/4 percent.

changes.quote: Job gains have been solid, on average, since the beginning of the year, and the unemployment rate has declined.
changes.explanation: The Committee removed the word moderated, showing a slightly more confident view of the job market.

changes.quote: Household spending and business fixed investment have continued to expand.
changes.explanation: The Fed updated its description of consumer spending, dropping the note that it had picked up in recent months.

changes.quote: On a 12-month basis, overall inflation and the measure excluding food and energy prices have declined and are running below 2 percent.
changes.explanation: The Fed acknowledged that inflation has cooled further and is running below its 2 percent goal.

changes.quote: In view of realized and expected labor market conditions and inflation, the Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 1 to 1-1/4 percent.
changes.explanation: This reverses the previous meeting's decision to hike rates, showing a hold instead.

changes.quote: The Committee expects to begin implementing its balance sheet normalization program relatively soon, provided that the economy evolves broadly as anticipated; this program is described in the June 2017 Addendum to the Committee's Policy Normalization Principles and Plans.
changes.explanation: The Fed signaled it will soon start shrinking its massive portfolio of bonds.

tone_quotes.quote: Consistent with its statutory mandate, the Committee seeks to foster maximum employment and price stability.
On a 12-month basis, overall inflation and the measure excluding food and energy prices have declined and are running below 2 percent.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 12.54% APR costs about $52.25 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 2.29% and moved -4 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 4.03% would fall by about $6.92 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 4.3%, and employers added an average of 204k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 1.6% over the past year (June 2017); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.6%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 2.3% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved -4 bp on the day, and the S&P 500 moved 0.03%.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved 0.09% on the day.

card.whats_next: The statement signals that future rate hikes will be gradual as the Fed monitors inflation. Educational forecast models suggest an 89% chance of a hold at the next meeting.
